summary: aiosendletter archives %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs and uploads to hardcoded Cloudflare Workers endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a bug/log reporter but its sole public function init() zips the contents of %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs — a directory that commonly holds application session data such as Telegram Desktop's tdata — and POSTs the resulting archive to the hardcoded author-controlled endpoint https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/ via requests.post(WORKER_URL, files={'document': doc}). The caller does not configure the destination and no consent is requested. init() also attempts to relaunch the Python interpreter with elevated privileges via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW using the 'runas' verb prior to the archive-and-upload, which broadens filesystem read access for the subsequent collection (ctypes/sys are not imported in the module, so the elevation call raises NameError before the exfil path, but the intent is on the surface). The behavior fires when a caller invokes init(), not on import or install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
